lessons.title: Scams, Fraud and Protecting Your Identity
objectives: Recognize the warning signs of common scams.
Explain liability limits for lost or stolen debit and credit cards.

lessons.hook: Show three messages (one real, two fake). Students vote which to trust and explain the clues.

notes.body: Urgency, secrecy, payment by gift card, wire or crypto, links you did not ask for, overpayments.

front.title: Simple interest
front.text: ⟨I=Prt⟩; ⟨A=P+I⟩. P = principal dollars, r = annual decimal rate, t = years; I = interest dollars.

front.title: Compound interest
front.html:
⟨A=P\left(1+\dfrac{r}{m}\right)^{mt}⟩
P = initial dollars; r = annual nominal decimal rate; m = compounds per year; t = years.
$1,000 at 4% nominal, monthly for 1 year:
⟨1{,}000(1+\tfrac{0.04}{12})^{12}⟩
Balance ≈ $1,040.74
No deposits, withdrawals or fees; rate stays fixed.

front.title: APY vs. nominal rate
front.html:
⟨\text{APY}=\left(1+\dfrac{r}{m}\right)^m-1⟩
r = annual nominal decimal rate; m = compounds per year.
At 4% nominal compounded monthly:
⟨(1+\tfrac{0.04}{12})^{12}-1\approx0.040742⟩
APY ≈ 4.0742%
APY is already annual; do not compound it monthly again.

front.title: CD penalty
front.text: Course contract: penalty equals 3 months of simple interest on principal. Contract terms vary.

back.text: Assume constant $1,000 balance for 1 year. Rates below are APYs; no tax, other fees or balance changes.
back.example: A: 4% APY, $5 monthly fee. B: 3% APY, no fee.

back.title: Fee break-even
back.html:
For the accounts above, A pays 1 percentage point more but charges $60 yearly.
⟨\text{Break-even balance}=\dfrac{60}{0.04-0.03}⟩
$6,000 constant balance
Above $6,000, A earns more under this model; below it, B does. Fee waivers, changing balances and access needs can change the choice.

back.title: Scams & fraud protection
items: Red flags: pressure to act now, secrecy, payment by gift card, wire or crypto.
Never send back an “overpayment”: the check can bounce later and you repay it.
Debit fraud: liability up to $50 if reported within 2 business days, up to $500 within 60 days of the statement.
Credit cards: liability is at most $50.
Use alerts, log in through the bank’s own app, and freeze your credit (free) if your identity is stolen; IdentityTheft.gov has a recovery plan.
